column1: MILE 12 WARRIOR  |  AEO / GEO Question Keywords — AI Citation Layer
Targets for ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. Answer-first blocks of 40-60 words immediately under each H2, then the depth.

column2: Question Keyword
column5: Answer Block Angle

column2: How many hours can a truck driver drive in a day?
column5: Lead with the number: 11 driving hours inside a 14-hour on-duty window after 10 consecutive off-duty. Then the exceptions. This is the single most-asked trucking question in AI chat.

column2: What is the 14-hour rule for truck drivers?
column5: Define the clock, state that it does not pause for breaks, give one worked example with times.

column2: What is the 30-minute break rule?
column5: Required after 8 cumulative driving hours; can be off-duty, sleeper, or on-duty not driving. Name the common mistake.

column2: How does the split sleeper berth rule work?
column5: Give the 8/2 and 7/3 splits in one sentence each, then a table of legal combinations.

column2: What are the warning signs of driver fatigue?
column5: Six-item list: lane drift, missed exits, heavy eyelids, repeated yawning, memory gaps, delayed reaction. Lists get lifted whole into AI answers.

column2: How do truck drivers stay awake on long hauls?
column5: Rank the tactics honestly and say which ones do not work. Contrarian accuracy earns citations.

column2: How long should a power nap be while driving?
column5: 20 minutes, why 30+ backfires, where to park safely.

column2: What is a coffee nap?
column5: Caffeine then immediate 20-minute nap; explain the 20-30 minute onset window.

column2: How much sleep does a truck driver need?
column5: 7-8 uninterrupted hours; address sleep debt accumulation across a week.

column2: How do you sleep better in a semi truck sleeper?
column5: Temperature, light blocking, noise, parking choice, wind-down sequence. Six concrete steps.

column2: Can you drive a truck with sleep apnea?
column5: Yes with treated and documented compliance; explain the examiner referral path.

column2: What percentage of truck drivers have sleep apnea?
column5: Cite the prevalence range and the source. Statistic pages get cited constantly by AI engines.

column2: How do truck drivers avoid back pain?
column5: Seat setup, 2-hour stop rule, three named stretches, cushion criteria.

column2: What exercises can you do in a truck cab?
column5: Six exercises with sets and reps, no equipment beyond a band.

column2: How much water should a truck driver drink?
column5: 64 oz baseline, the urine-colour check, why drivers under-drink.

column2: What can truck drivers eat that is healthy at truck stops?
column5: Name real chains and real items. Specificity is what beats generic wellness blogs.

column2: What blood pressure disqualifies a CDL driver?
column5: Give the tiered certification lengths by reading. Highly searched, poorly answered.

column2: How do I pass my DOT physical?
column5: Prep checklist for the 72 hours before, plus what is actually measured.

column2: Why are truck drivers more likely to be depressed?
column5: Isolation, irregular sleep, financial pressure, stigma. Cite the rate differential.

column2: How do truck drivers deal with loneliness?
column5: Scheduled contact, community, pets, routine. Give the daily 10-minute rule.

column2: Where can a truck driver get mental health help?
column5: 988, Crisis Text Line, SAMHSA, St. Christopher Fund. Named resources with numbers.

column2: How do you manage stress as a truck driver?
column5: 4-7-8 breathing at every fuel stop, plus four other in-cab techniques.

column2: What is a safe following distance for a semi truck?
column5: 7 seconds at highway speed, doubled in weather. Give the counting method.

column2: How often should a truck driver check mirrors?
column5: Every 5-8 seconds in a named scan order.

column2: What should you do if a steer tire blows out?
column5: Do not brake, accelerate slightly, hold the wheel, ease off. Three-step sequence.

column2: Should you use high beams in fog?
column5: No, and explain the reflection physics in one sentence.

column2: How do you drive safely on black ice?
column5: Speed reduction ratios, following distance, steer into the skid, where ice forms first.

column2: What are R1 R2 and R3 chain controls in California?
column5: Define all three levels plainly. Very few sites answer this cleanly.

column2: What should be in a truck breakdown kit?
column5: Nine-item list mapped to 49 CFR 393.95 requirements.

column2: How far behind the truck do warning triangles go?
column5: 10 ft, 100 ft, 200 ft. Add the divided-highway variation.

column2: What do you do first after a truck accident?
column5: Numbered eight-step sequence, safety before paperwork.

column2: What should a new truck driver expect in the first 90 days?
column5: Week-by-week arc with the three points where drivers quit.

column2: What are the most common rookie truck driver mistakes?
column5: Ten mistakes with the fix for each. Highly linkable.

column2: What should I pack for my first OTR run?
column5: Categorised list: sleep, food, hygiene, tools, documents, comfort.

column2: How do I talk to my dispatcher as a new driver?
column5: Give actual scripts. Scripts are the highest-value AI-citable format.

column2: What should be in a driver orientation packet?
column5: Section-by-section table of contents plus the DQ-file sign-off requirement.

column2: How often is driver refresher training required?
column5: Federal baseline vs insurer expectation vs best practice. Honest three-part answer.

column2: How can a fleet reduce driver turnover?
column5: Wellness, home time, communication, respect. Tie to retention data.

column2: How do you support a spouse who drives a truck?
column5: Practical and emotional. Almost nobody owns this answer today.

column2: How do truck drivers stay connected with their kids?
column5: Voice messages, shared albums, ritual calls, a shared journal.
